transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Um… I guess I’m here because I’ve been getting really stuck on how my face looks, especially now that I’m more in front of people for work. There’s this one part of my face that looks uneven to me in photos, and I keep staring at it even though other people say they can barely notice anything. I know that probably sounds kind of silly, but it’s been hard to stop thinking about.
Do you find yourself doing anything over and over to try to make yourself feel better about how your face looks?

Yeah… I mean, I try not to make a big deal of it, but I do check more than I probably should. Like before I send out event pictures or hop on a vendor meeting, I’ll look at my face in my phone camera a bunch, or retake the photo until it looks less… off.

Sometimes I tilt my head a certain way so it doesn’t show as much, and I’ll ask a coworker, like, “Do I look weird?” even though I know that’s probably annoying. It can take longer than I want to admit, and then I’m behind on actual planning stuff. I know that sounds kind of excessive.
Is this concern about your face affecting your daily life or relationships in a significant way?

Yeah… I mean, I wouldn’t say it’s ruining everything, but it has started getting in the way more than I want to admit. I actually missed part of a planning deadline because I spent so much time trying to deal with how I looked in the event materials, like checking and rechecking pictures and stuff.

And now vendor calls and meeting prep take me longer than they should, because I get caught up making sure my face looks okay first. I know that probably sounds dramatic, but… it does affect things.
Do you feel like you have to perform these checks or rituals in a specific way or a certain number of times?

Not like a specific number, I don’t think… it’s not like I have to do it five times or something. It’s more like I keep doing it until it looks “okay” enough, if that makes sense.

Like before sending event pictures or getting on a vendor meeting, I’ll check my face in my phone camera, retake the photo, tilt my head a certain way… and sometimes I’ll ask a coworker if I look weird. I know that probably sounds kind of unnecessary. It’s just hard to stop until I feel a little less uncomfortable, and then suddenly I’ve spent way too much time on it and I’m behind on planning stuff.
Is your concern mainly about how your face looks to others, or is it more about how it feels to you, like something is wrong with it?

It’s mostly about how it looks to other people, I think. Like… I came in because since I’ve had to be more in front of people at work, I keep noticing this one uneven-looking part of my face in photos.

I know other people say they barely see anything, so I feel kind of silly saying it, but once I see it, I can’t really stop staring at it. It just feels like that’s what everyone else must be noticing too, even if they say they’re not.
Do you think something bad would happen if you didn't check your face before sending out pictures or going on meetings?

I don’t think something really bad would happen, exactly… like, I know logically the meeting would still happen or the pictures would still go out.

But I get this feeling that if I don’t check first, I might miss something really obvious and then everyone will notice how weird my face looks. So before I send event pictures or join a vendor meeting, I’ll check my phone camera, maybe retake the photo, angle my head differently… sometimes I’ll ask a coworker if I look okay.

I know that probably sounds a little excessive. It just makes me feel safer, I guess, even though it can take long enough that I end up behind on planning stuff.
Do you feel like your face needs to look perfect or symmetrical for you to feel comfortable?

I wouldn’t say perfect, exactly… I know nobody’s face is perfectly symmetrical. But, um, yeah, I think I feel a lot more comfortable if that uneven part doesn’t stand out.

Since I’ve had to be more in front of people at work, especially in photos, I just keep noticing it. Even when people tell me they barely see anything, I’ll still stare at it and think, like, “No, it’s there.” I know that probably sounds dramatic, but it’s hard for me to let it go once I’ve seen it.
Do you think people are actually noticing this uneven part of your face, or is it more that you're worried about what they might think if they did notice?

I guess… I don’t totally know if they’re actually noticing it. People usually say they barely see anything, so I know maybe it’s more in my head than I want to admit.

But since I’ve had to be more in front of people at work, especially in photos, I just can’t stop staring at that one uneven-looking part of my face. And then I start thinking, if I can see it that clearly, they must be able to see it too… or they might notice it and think I look weird.

I’m sorry, I know that probably sounds kind of vain or silly. It’s just hard for me not to focus on it once I’ve seen it.
Do you feel like checking your face is something you need to do to prevent a specific bad outcome, or is it more about trying to feel better about how you look?

I think it’s more about trying to feel better, or like… less uncomfortable with how I look. I’m not really thinking, “If I don’t check, something terrible will happen.” It’s more that before I send event pictures or join a vendor meeting, I feel like I have to make sure my face doesn’t look weird.

So I’ll check it in my phone camera, retake photos, tilt my head a certain way… sometimes ask a coworker if I look okay. I know that probably sounds like a lot. It’s just supposed to make me feel calmer, but then it can take enough time that I fall behind on planning stuff.
Do you feel like you would still check your face repeatedly even if you knew for certain that it looked fine to others?

Probably… yeah. I mean, I’d like to say if I knew other people thought I looked fine, I’d just stop, but I don’t think it works that cleanly for me.

Before I send event pictures or get on a vendor meeting, I still end up checking my face in my phone camera, or retaking the picture, or turning my head a little to see if it looks better. Sometimes I’ll ask a coworker, like, “Do I look weird?” even if I’m pretty sure they’re going to say no.

It’s embarrassing to admit, because I know it can seem excessive. But it does take up time sometimes—enough that I fall behind on planning things I’m supposed to be doing.
Do you feel like you could stop checking your face if you really wanted to?

I mean… I think I could stop for a little bit if I really forced myself, maybe. But it feels really hard in the moment.

Like before I send event pictures or get on a vendor meeting, I’ll tell myself I’m just going to check once, and then I end up opening my phone camera again, retaking the photo, tilting my head different ways… or asking someone at work if I look weird. I know that probably sounds excessive, sorry.

It’s not like I want to be doing it. It just feels like I can’t quite let it go, and then sometimes it eats up enough time that I’m behind on the planning stuff I’m supposed to be doing.
Is your need to check your face more about making sure it looks symmetrical or more about fixing the specific part of your face that you think looks uneven?

Um… I think it’s more the specific part, honestly. Like, I don’t know if “fixing” is the right word, but I get stuck on this one area of my face that looks uneven to me in photos.

It got worse once I had to be more in front of people at work, like in event pictures or things like that. Other people say they barely notice anything, so I know maybe I’m making it into too much, but I still end up staring at it and trying to make it look… less uneven, I guess. Is that what you mean?
Do you feel like you're checking your face because of how it looks or because you feel like you have to check it?

I think it starts because of how it looks… like that uneven part just catches my attention and I feel like I need to make sure it isn’t showing too much.

But then it turns into this feeling like I have to check, if that makes sense. Like before I send event pictures or get on a vendor meeting, I’ll just look in my phone camera “one more time,” or retake it, or tilt my head a certain way. Sometimes I’ll ask a coworker if I look weird, which I know is probably annoying, or unnecessary.

It’s not constant all day or anything, but it can take longer than I mean for it to, and then I’m behind on planning stuff. Does that answer what you mean?
Do you feel like you're checking your face to make it look a certain way, or because you feel compelled to do so?

I think… probably both, but more like I feel compelled once it starts.

At first I’m trying to make it look a certain way, like if I’m sending event pictures or about to join a vendor meeting, I’ll check my face in the phone camera and try to tilt my head so that uneven part doesn’t show as much. But then it’s like I can’t just leave it there. I’ll retake photos, check again, or sometimes ask a coworker if I look weird.

I know that sounds like a lot. I’m not trying to be difficult or vain, it just kind of grabs me, and then I realize I’ve spent too much time on it and I’m behind on the planning stuff I was supposed to be doing.
Do you feel like you would still feel the need to check your face even if you were completely alone and there was no chance of anyone else seeing you?

Um… I think if I were completely alone and nobody was going to see me, it probably wouldn’t be as strong. Like, the worst of it is before I send event pictures or get on a vendor meeting, because I’m worried that uneven part is going to show.

That’s when I start checking my phone camera, retaking pictures, tilting my head, or asking a coworker if I look weird. I don’t mean for it to turn into a whole thing, but it can take up enough time that I fall behind on planning stuff. So… I guess it’s more tied to being seen, if that makes sense?
Do you feel like checking your face is something you do because of the way it looks, or is it something you feel you must do regardless of how it looks?

I think it’s because of the way it looks, mostly… like if I notice that uneven part, then I feel like I need to check it.

But once I start, it kind of turns into something I feel like I have to do. Before I send event pictures or join a vendor meeting, I’ll check my face in my phone camera, retake photos, tilt my head a certain way, or sometimes ask a coworker if I look weird. I know that probably sounds like too much, and I’m not trying to make it a big deal, but it can take up enough time that I end up behind on planning stuff. Is that what you mean?
Do you think you would still feel anxious or uncomfortable if you didn't check your face before an event or meeting, even if you knew you looked fine?

Yeah… I think I would. Even if someone told me I looked fine, I’d probably still feel kind of uncomfortable if I didn’t check.

It’s like before sending event pictures or getting on a vendor meeting, I feel better if I can just look once… but then it turns into checking my phone camera more than once, retaking a picture, tilting my head so it looks okay, or asking a coworker if I look weird. I know that sounds a little excessive. It just feels hard to move on without doing it, and sometimes I lose enough time that I’m behind on the planning work. Does that answer what you mean?
Do you think you would still feel the urge to check your face even if you were convinced that the uneven part you're worried about wasn't noticeable to others?

Yeah… I think maybe I still would, at least a little. Even if I really tried to believe it wasn’t noticeable, I’d still get that urge to just check quickly before I send event pictures or get on a vendor meeting.

And then sometimes “quickly” turns into me checking my phone camera a few times, retaking photos, tilting my head so it looks better, or asking a coworker if I look weird. I know that probably sounds like I’m overdoing it… but it can take enough time that I get behind on planning stuff. Is that what you mean?
Do you think your face would ever look okay to you if you didn't check it before an event or meeting?

I want to say yes, but honestly… probably not right away. If I don’t check before an event or a vendor meeting, my face doesn’t really feel “okay” to me. I keep thinking I should just look once in my phone camera, or retake a picture, or angle my head so it looks better.

Sometimes I’ll ask a coworker if I look weird, which I know is probably annoying or unnecessary. It’s not like I’m trying to waste time, but it can take longer than I mean it to and then I get behind on planning stuff. Does that make sense?
Do you think you would still feel the need to check your face if you were completely certain that there was nothing wrong with your appearance?

Yeah… I think I probably would, even if I knew nothing was actually wrong. I don’t know, it’s like I still need to check to feel settled.

Before I send event pictures or join a vendor meeting, I’ll look at my face in my phone camera, and sometimes I end up retaking photos or tilting my head a certain way so it looks better. Or I’ll ask a coworker if I look weird, even though I know that’s probably unnecessary.

I don’t mean for it to take long, but sometimes it kind of eats up time and then I’m behind on planning stuff. I hope that makes sense.
